customManagers.description: Talos version in versions.env -- the ONLY place this is tracked now. A Kustomize `replacements` block (config/kustomization.yaml) projects this into every SUC Plan's spec.version and talosctl image tag at build time, so there is no longer a separate manager for those; bumping this file is the whole update. The Factory installer tag in the machine configs (below) is the one pin Kustomize cannot reach and still needs its own manager. A bump here does NOT require regenerating SCHEMATIC_ID: the schematic ID is a content hash of the extension list and is independent of the Talos version -- the same ID serves v1.12.0 through v1.13.9. Only editing schematic.yaml changes it. The talos group is still never auto-merged, for the real reasons: the upgrade reboots nodes, and the Image Factory builds per (schematic, version) pair, so a brand-new release may have no image for these extensions yet. The Talos image workflow checks both.

Kubernetes control-plane/kubelet version in versions.env, upgraded independently of TALOS_VERSION via talosctl upgrade-k8s (plans/talos-kubernetes-upgrade.yaml). Grouped separately from talos and never auto-merged: the upgrade touches every node's control-plane components. This manager always proposes the newest kubernetes/kubernetes release it finds, with no notion of stepping one minor at a time -- Renovate has no setting for that on a raw regex-matched pin. talosctl upgrade-k8s only supports an N -> N or N -> N+1 minor step, so a PR from this manager that skips a minor is expected to fail the Talos image workflow's dedicated check, not something that check is a defensive fallback against.

Factory installer tag in the machine configs. Decides which Talos a rebuilt node installs, so leaving it behind versions.env means a rebuild lands on the old version and needs an immediate upgrade. This is the one pin Kustomize's replacements cannot reach: Talos machine config is applied by hand via talosctl, entirely outside Kustomize/Flux. The SCHEMATIC_ID in the same string is NOT tracked and must still be regenerated by hand whenever the schematic changes.

CloudNativePG cluster images using the stock cloudnative-pg/postgresql image. The built-in kubernetes manager only reads the `image:` key; CNPG Cluster resources spell it `imageName:`, so these pins (keycloak-pg, filer-meta-pg) were invisible to Renovate and drifted five patch releases behind -- 16.10 while 16.15 was current -- carrying 12 fixable critical CVEs between them. Every other image in the repo was kept current automatically; these were the ones nothing was watching. Immich's CNPG cluster uses a different image entirely (tensorchord/cloudnative-vectorchord) and has its own manager below, for the same reason this one exists but with different tag syntax.

Immich's CNPG database image, ghcr.io/tensorchord/cloudnative-vectorchord -- a different image from the CNPG manager above, which only matches cloudnative-pg/postgresql and has never matched this pin. Immich moved onto CNPG after that manager was written (#603), so this dependency has had no Renovate coverage since it started existing: the exact failure mode that manager's own description records for keycloak-pg/filer-meta-pg (patch releases behind, fixable critical CVEs accumulating), recurring for the cluster added after the fix. Found on code review (round 4). The tag is <postgres-major>-<vectorchord-version>, e.g. 17-0.3.0; versioningTemplate's `compatibility` capture group (a documented Renovate regex-versioning feature) keeps the postgres-major prefix fixed, so this only ever proposes a new VectorChord version for the SAME Postgres major -- never a cross-major jump, the same invariant the packageRule below enforces for the plain postgres image.

Path corrected 2026-09-20: the platform refactor moved this file to 16-immich/deferred/postgres-cluster.yaml without updating this manager, silently reopening the exact gap this manager exists to close -- found by checking every customManager's managerFilePatterns against the real tree rather than assuming a path written once still holds. keycloak's own postgres-cluster.yaml also moved to a deferred/ path, but needs no equivalent fix: it uses the stock cloudnative-pg/postgresql image, already covered regardless of location by the CNPG manager above's unscoped /cluster/base/infrastructure/.+\.yaml$/ pattern.

kubeopencode's three per-role agent images (agentImage, executorImage, attachImage) -- not `image:` keys, so the built-in kubernetes manager never reads them, and they have had zero Renovate coverage. Low priority: kubeopencode is currently parked (27-kubeopencode/config/kustomization.yaml -- the controller cannot run against this cluster's controller-runtime version), so nothing is actually deployed to bump, but tracking costs nothing and stops the pins drifting further behind the chart while it's blocked. Already covered by the existing kubeopencode packageRule below: its /^ghcr[.]io/kubeopencode// pattern matches all three depNames, so no new grouping rule is needed, only extraction.

cilium-cli image used by the Talos cilium-install inlineManifest, which installs the CNI at first boot before Flux exists. This was cilium-cli-ci:latest -- an unpinned rolling CI build -- until it went distroless and broke bootstrap outright: the Job's shell form could no longer start. Pinning it is what stops the bootstrap path drifting under us again. Same file as the installer tag above and the same caveat: applied by hand via talosctl, outside Kustomize and Flux.

Cilium version the bootstrap cilium install lays down. Deliberately tracked as the SAME dep as the 05-cilium HelmRelease chart (datasource helm, name cilium) so Renovate bumps both in one PR instead of letting them drift -- a mismatch means first boot installs one Cilium and Flux immediately upgrades it to another. The capture group omits the leading v so it matches the chart version exactly; the v stays literal in the file because the CLI flag requires it.

Pinned CI tool versions in .github/workflows, comment-driven like the Ansible manager. These are plain `curl` downloads of release binaries, so no built-in manager sees them. Before this existed the pins drifted by hand and two of them were not pins at all -- Trivy came from an install.sh on the main branch and yq from /releases/latest -- which made CI unreproducible and, in Trivy's case, executed unversioned remote code.

Immich's app image tag, overridden in the shared top-level controllers block (helmrelease.yaml) to run the real latest v2.x release independently of the chart's own stale appVersion default -- see that file's comment and docs/backlog.md. A bare `image: {tag: ...}` with no adjacent `repository:` is invisible to both the built-in kubernetes manager (needs a single combined repo:tag value) and the helm-values manager (needs repository+tag together): this had zero Renovate coverage until this manager, found on an audit of every HelmRelease-embedded image override in the repo (2026-09-19). Tracked against the app repo directly (github-releases), not one specific ghcr.io image, since server and machine-learning always share this one tag by construction. Grouped with the immich packageRule below so it lands in the same manual-review PR as the chart and the vectorchord DB image.

kubernetes-mcp-server's app image, values.image.version -- a non-standard field name (version, not tag), with no repository present either. The file's own 2026-08-14 security-review comment claims 'Renovate's docker datasource will now track and PR version bumps the same as every other pinned image in this repo' -- checked against the actual renovate.json on the same audit that found the immich gap above (2026-09-19): that claim was never true, nothing referenced this chart or field. Not grouped with the kubeopencode packageRule: quay.io/containers/kubernetes_mcp_server is an unrelated upstream project that happens to share this local namespace, not a kubeopencode release.

CNPG's Barman Cloud plugin controller image, plugin-barman-cloud.yaml's values.image.tag -- tag-only, no repository, and the file isn't named helmrelease.yaml so even the paired-field helm-values manager could never reach it regardless of shape. Found on the same 2026-09-19 audit as the immich and kubernetes-mcp-server gaps above. Repository confirmed live (kubectl get pod -n cnpg-system), not guessed. Grouped with the sidecar image below per this file's own comment: 'move both tags together, in a reviewed PR'.

CNPG's Barman Cloud plugin SIDECAR image, plugin-barman-cloud.yaml's values.sidecarImage.tag -- the highest-blast-radius of the three gaps found on this audit: this is the image injected into every CNPG database pod (keycloak-pg, filer-meta-pg, immich-pg), confirmed live via each pod's initContainers, not the controller deployment. Same tag-only/wrong-filename problem as the controller image above, and the same fix.

packageRules.description: Keep CloudNativePG on the PostgreSQL 16 series. A major version change there is a database upgrade with its own migration path, not an image bump, and must never arrive as an automated PR.

The built-in kubernetes manager line-matches every `image:` field in any /cluster/.+\.yaml$ file regardless of `kind:`, so without this it independently proposes bumps to the talosctl image tags inside the SUC Plan files (talos-controlplane/worker/on-demand/kubernetes-upgrade.yaml). Those are Kustomize `replacements` placeholders now (config/kustomization.yaml), not pins -- a bump from this manager would edit a value that gets overwritten at build time anyway, in an ungrouped PR unrelated to the versions.env-driven update.

The built-in kubernetes manager treats machine.install.image (factory.talos.dev/installer/<schematic-hash>:<tag>) as a plain Docker image and tries to list its tags. That always fails -- the schematic hash is a content hash, not a browsable repository -- so the Dependency Dashboard carries a permanent 'could not be looked up' warning for a dependency the siderolabs/talos custom manager above already tracks correctly by the real value (the tag, not the hash).

Two earlier fixes for this, each merged and confirmed NOT to clear the warning by checking the live dashboard afterward: (1) a negative managerFilePatterns entry excluding controlplane.yaml from the manager's file match -- did nothing, because managerFilePatterns is `mergeable: true` in Renovate's own option schema (lib/config/options/index.ts): user config MERGES with a built-in manager's default file match rather than replacing it, so no entry in this field, positive or negative, can ever remove a file the manager already covers by default. (2) A packageRule matching matchFileNames + enabled:false (this rule's own previous shape) -- also did nothing: it stops an update from being proposed, but not the lookup that populates this specific warning.

What actually works, matching a maintainer-confirmed fix for this exact warning shape (renovatebot/renovate#30889) and this repo's own live test: matchManagers + matchPackageNames on the literal depName, not the file. packageRules apply 'pre-lookup' once the depName is known, and depConfig.enabled === false at that point skips the datasource call entirely (lib/workers/repository/process/fetch.ts) -- matchFileNames evidently doesn't reach that same pre-lookup gate for this manager, matchPackageNames does. The schematic hash below must be updated by hand if the schematic ever changes (schematic.yaml) -- the same maintenance burden the custom regex managers above already carry for this same hash.

Block system-upgrade-controller chart 110.0.0 -- it is WITHDRAWN. It was published once, applied here as Helm release .v3, and pulled from https://rancher.github.io/charts afterwards. The index now carries 17 versions, newest 109.0.2. Flux cannot resolve it: the HelmChart sits Stalled on 'no chart with version matching 110.0.0 found', and a stalled chart cannot re-render, so every change to that HelmRelease applies cleanly to the object and silently never reaches the cluster (see #396). Renovate keeps offering it because it tracks the GitHub repo, where the tag still exists, rather than the chart index -- so the version it proposes is one that cannot be installed. Excluded as a semver range with a hole rather than a ceiling, so a genuine 110.0.1 is still offered if Rancher republishes -- pinning below 110 would silently freeze this chart at 109 forever.

Group the CLUSTER's Talos updates into one PR: versions.env's TALOS_VERSION and the machineconfig installer tag. Those two must move together -- talos-image-check fails a PR where they disagree -- so splitting them would produce a PR that fails its own check. The talosctl IMAGE in the SUC Plans needs no manager of its own: it is the same Kustomize-replacements field as TALOS_VERSION (see config/kustomization.yaml), so it cannot drift. The workstation talosctl BINARY in bootstrap/ is deliberately NOT in this group -- see the talos-cli rule at the end of this list.
Kubernetes control-plane version -- tracked and upgraded independently of Talos, never auto-merged (control-plane component upgrade).
Label major updates — CI workflow uses this to skip Trivy auto-merge
Label minor/patch updates — CI Trivy gate evaluates auto-merge eligibility
Disable digest updates for Talos images

Group Flux updates. helm/helm (the standalone Helm CLI installed in trivy-auto-patch.yml/trivy-automerge.yml for chart rendering, comment-pinned in .github/workflows) joins this group rather than staying on its own independent latest-upstream schedule: it exists to render charts the way this cluster's Flux actually does, so its version is only meaningful relative to what helm-controller vendors, not upstream helm/helm's own release cadence. Checked 2026-09-19 (PR #634 -- Renovate proposing v3->v4 independently -- prompted the check): the currently-pinned helm-controller v1.6.4 already vendors helm.sh/helm/v4 v4.2.4 (confirmed against its go.mod), so v4 is not ahead of the cluster, it matches it -- but that was a fact to verify, not assume, and the only way to keep it a checked fact going forward is to stop letting this update independently and force it into the same reviewed PR as the next helm-controller/flux2 bump, at which point the reviewer re-checks the new version's go.mod the same way before choosing a CLI version to match.
Route all patch updates through Trivy gate (no Renovate-side automerge)

Split the admin workstation's talosctl CLI out of the cluster Talos group. bootstrap/ansible/group_vars/all.yml pins a BINARY downloaded onto a laptop (roles/homelab-tools fetches talosctl-{os}-{arch} from the release). That is a different artifact from the cluster's OS version, it touches no node, and it cannot break an upgrade. The rule grouping all siderolabs/talos updates has a rationale written about the ghcr.io/siderolabs/talosctl IMAGE in the SUC Plans -- which genuinely is driven by the same Kustomize replacement as TALOS_VERSION. The workstation binary was swept in only because it resolves to the same GitHub release. Talos supports client/server skew (a reboot on 2026-09-05 printed 'server version 1.13.0 is older than client version 1.13.6' as a normal warning), so these need not move together -- and bundling them puts a laptop tool bump in the same PR that reboots the cluster.

Never bump the postgres backup client across a major. These three images run pg_dump against keycloak-pg, filer-meta-pg and immich-postgresql, and each must match its server's major: pg_dump emits SQL for its OWN version, with no target-version flag and no down-conversion, so a dump taken by a newer client can fail to replay into an older server. On 2026-09-05 Renovate moved all three to 18 -- two majors ahead of two of the servers. Nothing caught it, because the DUMP direction kept working and the read-back checks kept passing; the failure would have appeared for the first time during an actual restore. Renovate cannot know these versions are coupled to a server it never sees, so the coupling is enforced here. Patch and minor updates within the pinned major still flow normally.

Never auto-merge a VectorChord bump, including a plain semver 'minor' one. postgres-cluster.yaml's own comment says Immich manages this extension itself and updates it on startup -- the deployed Immich version decides which VectorChord versions it accepts, a coupling Renovate cannot see from the tag alone. Grouped with the immich chart so both land in front of the same review rather than the image quietly auto-merging through the Trivy gate's minor-update path (found on code review, round 4, after a real minor bump -- 17-0.3.0 to 17-0.5.3 -- checked against the actual tag list). immich-app/immich (the app image tag override, added 2026-09-19) joins the same group for the same reason: a new app version and a new chart version are the same underlying decision and must not land as two independent, unreviewed-together PRs.

CNPG's Barman Cloud plugin controller and sidecar images move as one -- plugin-barman-cloud.yaml's own comment: 'the sidecar is what runs inside every database pod, so a bump to it restarts each database once: move both tags together, in a reviewed PR.' Neither had any Renovate coverage until the two custom managers above; grouping them now, at the same time coverage starts, so they can never land as two separate PRs on two separate days.

docker.io/rancher/kuberlr-kubectl is pinned independently in four unrelated files (05-cilium/bootstrap-rbac-cleanup.yaml and three system-upgrade-controller/kubescape cronjobs) -- each already tracked individually by the built-in kubernetes manager, but with no relationship between them a bump can land in one file's PR and not the other three, leaving the cluster running several different kubectl-wrapper versions for the same purpose with no reason. Grouped so every occurrence moves together in one PR. docker.io/library/python is deliberately NOT grouped the same way -- different services, different upgrade cadence, no shared-version rationale the way this single-purpose kubectl wrapper has.

Never auto-merge the components that cannot be recovered from inside the cluster (ADR-009). A bad image in the network layer, the storage layer or remote access removes the means of fixing it: no CNI means no scheduling, no CSI means no volumes, and no Tailscale means no remote path in once the LAN one is gone. Size of the version step is irrelevant -- a patch can break a datapath as thoroughly as a major. manual-review is the label the Trivy auto-merge gate already refuses on, so this reuses that mechanism rather than adding one.

Kyverno ships five images from one release -- four controllers plus the admission init container -- and the chart that wires them. ADR-009 requires they move as one change: a deployment running mismatched Kyverno components is a worse failure than one that is a version behind.

Tailscale's operator and proxy images ship as one release, with the chart. Grouped so they cannot diverge. Also carries manual-review from the unrecoverable-component rule -- losing the operator removes the remote path into the cluster.
kubeopencode's controller and server are two roles of one binary, pinned twice from the same repository. Grouped so a bump cannot land on one and not the other.

SeaweedFS ships as two separately-tracked packages that are really one release: the chart (01-seaweedfs/helmrelease.yaml) and the chrislusf/seaweedfs image the collection-routing Job pins for itself (cluster/overlays/1-node/seaweedfs-collection-routing-job.yaml, a different file, so the matchFileNames grouping style used elsewhere in this list does not reach it). Ungrouped, client (the Job) and server (the chart) can land on different days in different PRs and drift apart -- the same class of problem the file-based chart+image groups below exist to prevent. Found on code review (round 4).

Longhorn's ten images move as one group. The four longhorn-* images are one release, and the six CSI sidecars are republished by longhornio and version-matched to it -- upstream csi-attacher and Longhorn's build of it are not interchangeable. A CSI driver assembled from mismatched sidecars fails at volume attach, which here means every workload with a PVC. Also carries manual-review from the unrecoverable-component rule.

Move the victoria-metrics chart and its pinned images together. ADR-009 requires a chart and the images it packages to move in one change. The chart's appVersion and the pinned tags describe the same release, so a proposal that carries one without the other opens a window where the pin is a downgrade of the chart's own intent. Grouping by package file keeps them in a single branch whenever both updates are available together.
Move the grafana chart and its pinned images together. See the victoria-metrics rule above for the reasoning; ADR-009 requires this for every chart.
